{{Short description|Telecommunication formula by Harald T. Friis}}
{{Distinguish|Friis transmission equation}}

{{No footnotes|date=May 2023}}
'''Friis formula''' or '''Friis's formula''' (sometimes '''Friis' formula'''), named after Danish-American electrical engineer [[Harald T. Friis]], is either of two formulas used in [[telecommunications engineering]] to calculate the [[signal-to-noise ratio]] of a multistage [[amplifier]]. One relates to [[noise factor]] while the other relates to [[noise temperature]].

==The Friis formula for noise factor==
[[File:Frijs-Kette.svg|Amplifier chain with known power gain factors ''G''<sub>1,2,3</sub> und noise factors ''F''<sub>1,2,3</sub>.]]

Friis's formula is used to calculate the total [[noise factor]] of a cascade of stages, each with its own [[noise factor]] and [[Gain (electronics)|power gain]] (assuming that the impedances are matched at each stage). The total [[noise factor]] can then be used to calculate the total [[noise figure]].  The total [[noise factor]] is given as

{{Equation box 1
|indent =
|title=
|equation = <math>F_\text{total} = F_1 + \frac{F_2-1}{G_1} + \frac{F_3-1}{G_1 G_2} + \frac{F_4-1}{G_1 G_2 G_3} + \cdots + \frac{F_n - 1}{G_1 G_2 \cdots G_{n-1}}</math>
|cellpadding= 6
|border
|border colour = #0073CF
|background colour=#F5FFFA}}

where <math>F_i</math> and <math>G_i</math> are the noise factor and available [[power gain]], respectively, of the ''i''-th stage, and ''n'' is the number of stages. Both magnitudes are expressed as ratios, not in decibels. 

===Consequences===
An important consequence of this formula is that the overall noise figure of a [[radio receiver]] is primarily established by the noise figure of its first amplifying stage.  Subsequent stages have a diminishing effect on [[signal-to-noise ratio]].  For this reason, the first stage amplifier in a receiver is often called the [[low-noise amplifier]] (LNA). The overall receiver noise "factor" is then

:<math>F_\mathrm{receiver} = F_\mathrm{LNA} + \frac{F_\mathrm{rest}-1}{G_\mathrm{LNA}}</math>

where <math>F_\mathrm{rest}</math> is the overall noise factor of the subsequent stages. According to the equation, the overall noise factor, <math>F_\mathrm{receiver}</math>, is dominated by the noise factor of the LNA, <math>F_\mathrm{LNA}</math>, if the gain is sufficiently high. The resultant Noise Figure expressed in dB is:
:<math>\mathrm{NF}_\mathrm{receiver}=10 \log(F_\mathrm{receiver})</math>

===Derivation===
For a derivation of Friis' formula for the case of three cascaded amplifiers (<math>n=3</math>) consider the image below.
[[File:FriiNoiseFormula.svg|Chain of three amplifiers]]

A source outputs a signal of power <math>S_i</math> and noise of power <math>N_i</math>. Therefore the SNR at the input of the receiver chain is <math>\text{SNR}_i = S_i/N_i</math>. The signal of power <math>S_i</math> gets amplified by all three amplifiers. Thus the signal power at the output of the third amplifier is <math>S_o = S_i \cdot G_1 G_2 G_3</math>. The noise power at the output of the amplifier chain consists of four parts:
*The amplified noise of the source (<math>N_i \cdot G_1 G_2 G_3</math>)
*The output referred noise of the first amplifier <math>N_{a1}</math> amplified by the second and third amplifier (<math>N_{a1} \cdot G_2 G_3</math>)
*The output referred noise of the second amplifier <math>N_{a2}</math> amplified by the third amplifier (<math>N_{a2} \cdot G_3</math>)
*The output referred noise of the third amplifier <math>N_{a3}</math>
Therefore the total noise power at the output of the amplifier chain equals
:<math>N_o = N_i G_1 G_2 G_3 + N_{a1} G_2 G_3 + N_{a2} G_3 + N_{a3}</math>
and the SNR at the output of the amplifier chain equals
:<math>\text{SNR}_o = \frac{S_i G_1 G_2 G_3}{N_i G_1 G_2 G_3 + N_{a1} G_2 G_3 + N_{a2} G_3 + N_{a3}}</math>.
The total noise factor may now be calculated as quotient of the input and output SNR:
:<math>F_\text{total} = \frac{\text{SNR}_i}{\text{SNR}_o} = \frac{\frac{S_i}{N_i}}{\frac{S_i G_1 G_2 G_3}{N_i G_1 G_2 G_3 + N_{a1} G_2 G_3 + N_{a2} G_3 + N_{a3}}} = 1 + \frac{N_{a1}}{N_i G_1} + \frac{N_{a2}}{N_i G_1 G_2} + \frac{N_{a3}}{N_i G_1 G_2 G_3}</math>
Using the definitions of the noise factors of the amplifiers we get the final result:
:<math>F_\text{total} = \underbrace{1 + \frac{N_{a1}}{N_i G_1}}_{=F_1} + \underbrace{\frac{N_{a2}}{N_i G_1 G_2}}_{=\frac{F_2-1}{G_1}} + \underbrace{\frac{N_{a3}}{N_i G_1 G_2 G_3}}_{=\frac{F_3-1}{G_1 G_2}} = F_1 + \frac{F_2-1}{G_1} + \frac{F_3-1}{G_1 G_2}</math>.


General derivation for a cascade of <math>n</math> amplifiers:

The total noise figure is given as the relation of the signal-to-noise ratio at the cascade input <math>\mathrm{SNR_i}=\frac{S_\mathrm{i}}{N_\mathrm{i}}</math> to the signal-to-noise ratio at the cascade output <math>\mathrm{SNR_o}=\frac{S_\mathrm{o}}{N_\mathrm{o}}</math> as

<math>F_{\mathrm{total}}=\frac{\mathrm{SNR_{i}}}{\mathrm{SNR_{o}}}=\frac{S_\mathrm{i}}{S_\mathrm{o}}\frac{N_\mathrm{o}}{N_\mathrm{i}}</math>.

The total input power of the <math>k</math>-th amplifier in the cascade (noise and signal) is <math>S_{k-1}+N_{k-1}</math>. It is amplified according to the amplifier's power gain <math>G_k</math>. Additionally, the amplifier adds noise with power <math>N_{\mathrm{a},k}</math>. Thus the output power of the <math>k</math>-th amplifier is <math>G_k \left( S_{k-1}+N_{k-1} \right) + N_{\mathrm{a},k}</math>. For the entire cascade, one obtains the total output power 

<math>S_\mathrm{o} + N_\mathrm{o} = \left( \left( \left( \left( S_{\mathrm{i}}+N_{\mathrm{i}} \right) G_1 + N_{\mathrm{a},1} \right) G_2 + N_{\mathrm{a},2} \right) G_3 + N_{\mathrm{a},3} \right) G_4 + \dots</math>

The output signal power thus rewrites as

<math>S_\mathrm{o}=S_\mathrm{i}\prod_{k=1}^{n} G_k</math>

whereas the output noise power can be written as

<math>N_\mathrm{o} = N_\mathrm{i} \prod_{k=1}^{n}G_k+\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}N_{\mathrm{a},k} \prod_{l=k+1}^{n}{G_l} + N_{\mathrm{a},n}

</math>

Substituting these results into the total noise figure leads to

<math>F_\mathrm{total}=\frac{N_\mathrm{i} \prod_{k=1}^{n}G_k+\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}N_{\mathrm{a},k} \prod_{l=k+1}^{n}{G_l} + N_{\mathrm{a},n}}{N_\mathrm{i}\prod_{k=1}^{n} G_k} = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{n-1} \frac{N_{\mathrm{a},k} \prod_{l=k+1}^{n}{G_l}}{N_\mathrm{i}\prod_{m=1}^{n} G_m}+ \frac{N_{\mathrm{a},n}}{N_\mathrm{i}\prod_{k=1}^{n} G_k} = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{n-1} \frac{N_{\mathrm{a},k}}{N_\mathrm{i}\prod_{m=1}^{k} G_m}+ \frac{N_{\mathrm{a},n}}{N_\mathrm{i}\prod_{k=1}^{n} G_k}

</math>

<math>= 1 + \frac{N_{\mathrm{a},1}}{N_\mathrm{i}G_1} + \sum_{k=2}^{n-1} \frac{N_{\mathrm{a},k}}{N_\mathrm{i}\prod_{m=1}^{k} G_m}+ \frac{N_{\mathrm{a},n}}{N_\mathrm{i}\prod_{k=1}^{n} G_k}

</math>

Now, using <math>F_k=1+\frac{N_{\mathrm{a},k}}{N_\mathrm{i}G_k}

</math> as the [[noise figure]] of the individual <math>k

</math>-th amplifier, one obtains

<math>F_\mathrm{total} = F_1 + \sum_{k=2}^{n} \frac{F_k -1}{\prod_{l=1}^{k-1} G_l}

</math>

<math>= F_1 + \frac{F_2 - 1}{G_1} + \frac{F_3 - 1}{G_1 G_2} + \frac{F_4 - 1}{G_1 G_2 G_3} + \dots + \frac{F_n - 1}{G_1 G_2 \dots G_{n-1}}

</math>

==The Friis formula for noise temperature==

Friis's formula can be equivalently expressed in terms of [[noise temperature]]:

{{Equation box 1
|indent =
|title=
|equation = <math>T_\text{eq} = T_1 + \frac{T_2}{G_1} + \frac{T_3}{G_1 G_2} + \cdots</math>
|cellpadding= 6
|border
|border colour = #0073CF
|background colour=#F5FFFA}}
